title: a question's key is re-keyed, not closed gap-gone and reopened, when the plan stops truncating it
line: a conflict's key is its whole detail, never a 120-character prefix; a row a run before this fix left under the old truncated key is found again by its full detail and re-keyed onto it, so a question the owner dismissed under the old key stays dismissed, never silently reopened as a new row

steps.say: the 1940 page arrives; the son and mother accepted first, so the father's own card can be
the father accepted: his birthplace disagrees with the file's own claim, a conflict whose detail is well over 120 characters

has: Pennsylvania against Northampton, Hampshire, Massachusetts, USA

steps.say: the plan opens the conflict at its full, untruncated key

expect.why: one row, open, at whatever key this run gave it

steps.say: the owner dismisses it, and the catalog is put back as a run before this fix would have left it: the same row, under the 120-character prefix the old q_key truncated to, closed and dismissed

set.q_key: conflict:birth place: United States, Census, 1940 (1,2442::26440834) against the file: Pennsylvania against Northampton, Hampshir

steps.say: the plan regenerated finds the dismissed row by its old, truncated key and re-keys it onto the full detail: it is not reopened, and no second row is created beside it

expect.why: one row only: re-keyed, never duplicated
still closed: a dismissed question stays dismissed
